appraisal_events.evidence: "même un homme de génie de qui nous attendons... le secret de l'infini, prononce seulement ces paroles, les mêmes qui venaient de sortir des lèvres de Bloch : « Qu'on fasse attention à mon chapeau haut de forme. »"
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator singles out Bloch's own vain remark about his hat as the exemplar of the trivial banality that even a supposed genius utters, an ironic deflation of him at the close of the scene.

status_effects.explanation: Bloch's closing remark is held up by the narrator as an example of vapid, self-regarding speech, mildly diminishing him despite his prominent presence in the scene.

ambiguities: The passage's extended meditation on Bloch's Jewish appearance (compared to Assyrian scribes, an animalizing hyena image, yet also 'admirable puissance de la race') is deeply ambivalent between aesthetic admiration and exoticizing othering; it was left unscored as essayistic/reflective description rather than a clean local social event, but a case could be made for either a positive (prestige via ancient/artistic association) or negative (discredit via animalization and reduction to spectacle) reading.

The candidate 'le grand-père du narrateur' does not actually appear in this passage: the 'mon grand-père' in the closing anecdote belongs to Mme de Villeparisis's own reported reminiscence about her own family, not the narrator's grandfather, so this candidate was not scored.
